<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to pick correct statement about DigiRL framework's interaction with the emulator.

Let's parse each option.

A: "In the Web Shopping subsets, DigiRL increased by 3.6% compared to Filtered BC, while in the General subsets it was about 10%." This is about improvement percentages. We saw from experiment: "DigiRL significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art agents ... achieving 49.5% absolute improvement – from 17.7 to 67.2% success rate – over supervised fine‑tuning...". In Table 1: For General test, Filtered BC offline-to-online: 61.5% success, DigiRL offline-to-online: 71.9% success. That's an increase of 10.4% (approx). For Web Shopping: Filtered BC offline-to-online: 57.8% success, DigiRL offline-to-online: 68.2% success. That's an increase of 10.4% as well. So not 3.6% in Web Shopping. So A is false.

B: "The all possible actions for the agent in the DigiRL framework include tapping and swiping on the screen using normalized (x, y) coordinates and typing variable-length text inputs." The action space described earlier: "available actions include tapping and sliding based on normalized (x, y) coordinates (ranging from 0 to 1 relative to the screen dimensions), typing text strings of variable length, and pressing special buttons such as HOME, BACK, and ENTER." So yes includes tapping and sliding (swiping) and typing variable-length text inputs. So B is correct.

C: "The automatic curriculum in DigiRL adjusts the instruction-level value function to filter out easy tasks, allowing the agent to focus solely on tasks it has not yet encountered during training." Actually, automatic curriculum uses instruction-level value function to prioritize tasks that have high advantage (i.e., low value) to maximize learning signal. It filters top-p datapoins with highest Ainstruct. It doesn't filter out easy tasks; It selects tasks with high advantage, meaning tasks that were harder (higher reward) or that the agent hasn't learned. So statement says "filter out easy tasks, allowing the agent to focus solely on tasks it has not yet encountered during training." Might be partially correct? But "not yet encountered" maybe not. The goal is to prioritize tasks with high advantage, not necessarily those it hasn't encountered. So statement is somewhat inaccurate. So C is false.

D: "The cross-entropy loss function is applied in DigiRL exclusively to the policy network, avoiding its use in the training of value functions to prevent overfitting in the model." Actually, cross-entropy loss is used for value functions, not policy. The policy uses MLE with log likelihood. They use cross-entropy for value functions and step-level value. So D is false.

Thus only B is correct. So answer is B.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{B}
